6hr6oelkmctl8q8146fijjlhu2.value: Credits: Tumble is our own game in the match-3 genre, which began with Eugene Alemzhin's Shariki (1994) and was made popular by PopCap's Bejeweled (2001) (prior art); Ersagun calls the question it shows "the Candy Crush problem", after King's Candy Crush Saga (2012). Steps kept in a queue and shown one at a time is the event queue pattern, as Robert Nystrom describes it in Game Programming Patterns (influence). New pieces come from Park and Miller's minimal standard random number generator (1988) (adaptation). Effects answered by handlers you choose, and a handler that keeps the rest of a computation to resume later: prior art in Eff (Bauer and Pretnar), Koka (Leijen) and OCaml 5's effects. The rules, the page and its handlers are ours.

fvvp4l7s7scskgbf8fc2c510b3.value: Tumble: one chain reaction, three ways to show it

cf7s2purln6k8nhta6dos4sl8s.value: Tap a piece, then a neighbour, to swap them. A line of three or more of a kind clears; the pieces above fall, new ones drop in, and the new board may match again: a chain reaction. Every step is animated, and animations take time. What should a tap do while they run? Your taps go to all three boards at the same moment. Try Two quick moves, or tap again while pieces are still falling.

djt1g6k981vpsg0k5vu9nrmv0u.value: Taps are ignored until the animation ends. Simple, and it is what the board shows, but the player waits.

h4h2pblvds54q91q0djs7cfm54.value: The whole chain is worked out the moment you swap; the logical board jumps to the end and the steps are queued to show. A tap meanwhile acts on that final board, which may not be what you see.

a0shgphqu1mmdgbenr4u5iuetp.value: The rules stop at each step (the handler parks the rest) and go on only when the step has been shown. A swap tapped meanwhile goes in between links, so it joins the chain reaction on the board you see.

a6u9peluoi4imfrpnsfovqda9h.value: The rules are written once (move and cascade). They perform Animate after every step, saying what happened and the board it left, and go on from the board the answer gives. They handle nothing themselves.

sj0j40oh00sgtmlri0imb3e1i0.value: Wait and All at once handle Animate with at once: every step is answered at once and collected as a list, shown afterwards from a queue. Step by step handles it with parked: the first step comes back with the rest of the chain, which the page resumes when the browser says that step's animation has ended (animationend), answering with the board as it is then.
